questions.q: In supervised learning, as described in the lesson, what is a label?
options: The file name given to a dataset before upload
A physical sticker placed on server hardware
The correct-answer tag paired with an example that the model learns to predict
The version number of the model's training code
questions.explain: The lesson defines a label as the correct-answer tag paired with training examples, which the model learns to predict for new data.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say labeling is where the most direct human judgment enters a model?
options: Labeling is always performed automatically by software with no human involvement
Labels are assigned randomly and have no connection to human opinion
Two labelers can reasonably disagree on an ambiguous case, and whichever judgment gets recorded becomes the model's treated-as-objective truth
Models are incapable of learning from any labeled data
questions.explain: The lesson explains that a labeler's judgment call becomes, for the model, the ground truth for that example — connecting directly to label bias.

questions.q: What does low inter-rater agreement signal, according to the lesson?
options: That the labelers used different computer operating systems
That the model has already finished training successfully
That the labeling task itself may be ambiguous, or the instructions given to labelers weren't clear enough
That the dataset is definitely too small to use
questions.explain: The lesson states low agreement between labelers is worth investigating as a sign of task ambiguity or unclear instructions.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say labeling instructions deserve to be treated as a governed document?
options: Because only software, never people, can follow labeling instructions
Because instructions never need to be written down at all
Because instructions are legally required to be printed on paper
Because they function almost like a policy, determining in practice what the model will learn to treat as true
questions.explain: The lesson draws a direct comparison between labeling instructions and policy documents, given their outsized influence on what the model learns.

questions.q: What is 'label provenance,' per the lesson?
options: The documented trail of which labeler or process produced a given label, and under what instructions
The total number of labels applied to a dataset
The geographic location where a labeling company is headquartered
A legal certificate proving a dataset is copyright-free
questions.explain: The lesson defines label provenance as traceability of a specific label back to its source labeler or process and instruction version.
